7ec58858d3.q: What are the main benefits of 5G technology according to AT&T engineers?
7ec58858d3.a: 5G supports a wide range of spectrum including millimeter wave frequencies from 24 to 300 gigahertz, providing speeds of 10 to 20 gigabit per second. It enables network slicing to provide specific services to public safety, healthcare, and industry without segments mixing. 5G also offers very low latency of about one to two milliseconds, enabling near real-time communication for video transmission and Internet of Things applications.

95bc81ea3a.q: What is the difference between 4G and 5G cellular networks in terms of architecture?
95bc81ea3a.a: 4G collapsed voice and data into one complete IP network with no circuit switching, making it function more like the internet. 5G builds on this foundation with higher data rates and the ability to slice networks for specific purposes, whereas 3G used two separate networks—one for voice and one for data—which was costly for providers.

5496931dcd.q: Is 5G radiation harmful to human health?
5496931dcd.a: The spectrum used for 5G is non-ionizing radiation, not ionizing radiation, so it does not provide any negative effects on users. While people may fear that propagating signals at high frequency generates ionized signals that could interfere with health, there are two types of radiation and 5G operates on the safe, non-ionizing type.

a924e25b65.q: How did Usang Ekpe win the 2022 Dr. James Mitchell Legacy Award?
a924e25b65.a: Ekpe was nominated by his director at AT&T for the award and informed on October 26, 2021 that he won the Dr. James W. Mitchell Legacy Award. He believes he was nominated partly because when AT&T brought in international employees during a time when outsourcing was unpopular, he transferred his knowledge to a group of college students outside the country rather than viewing it as a threat to his job.

2197f315a0.q: What is the history of cellular mobile phone technology from 1G to 5G?
2197f315a0.a: The first cellular phone call was made by Dr. Martin Cooper in 1973 in New York. 1G was introduced in 1981 and used analog technology with mechanical switches enabling only voice calls. 2G supported voice with limited data starting in 1992 with text messaging. 3G enabled voice and data but used two separate networks. 4G collapsed these into one IP network. 5G was introduced around 2018 with significantly higher data rates and new use cases.

c206ac207f.q: Why did Usang Ekpe choose telecommunications engineering over petroleum engineering?
c206ac207f.a: At a career day in high school, a general manager from Nigeria's analog telecommunication company spoke about using mechanical analog switches to enable long-distance communication, which captivated Ekpe. He also recognized that electrical and electronics engineering is more dynamic than petroleum engineering, with new developments or improvements emerging every one to two years, and he prefers doing different things rather than repeating the same work.

39719c14f0.q: What is the mission of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory and what role does the Buildings Program play?
39719c14f0.a: The National Renewable Energy Laboratory is one of 17 Department of Energy national laboratories and is the only one fully committed to a mission of a clean and energy efficient and renewable energy future. Dr. Jackson manages the program that supports the Building Technologies Office at Department of Energy, ensuring resources are delivered on time and on budget while bringing science and research strategies to identify what's next in clean energy and buildings work.
39719c14f0.e: High-Tech Sunday: Ep. 52 - Roderick Jackson, Ph.D.

43ed466bd1.q: How did Dr. Roderick Jackson combine his family's construction legacy with mechanical engineering and energy research?
43ed466bd1.a: Dr. Jackson leveraged his family's building construction legacy by integrating it with his engineering and science background. His father was a framer and all 11 of his father's brothers built houses. Rather than abandoning this legacy, Dr. Jackson brought engineering and science perspectives to take it to another level, eventually focusing his PhD research on energy in buildings—creating a marriage of family legacy with his passion for science and energy.
43ed466bd1.e: High-Tech Sunday: Ep. 52 - Roderick Jackson, Ph.D.

d769d6fdf2.q: What sparked Dr. Roderick Jackson's interest in energy research during his engineering education?
d769d6fdf2.a: Dr. Jackson's interest in energy was sparked in his senior design capstone course at Georgia Tech in 1996, taught by a professor who had been influential in designing the Olympic torch for the Atlanta Olympics. The professor focused heavily on energy, discussing peak oil and the importance of energy, which piqued Jackson's initial interest in pursuing a career in energy alongside his existing passion for thermodynamics.
d769d6fdf2.e: High-Tech Sunday: Ep. 52 - Roderick Jackson, Ph.D.

149cd7c087.q: How does Dr. Roderick Jackson integrate social justice and civil rights principles into clean energy work?
149cd7c087.a: Dr. Jackson was influenced by his mother's participation in the Civil Rights Movement and her emphasis on social justice. He now brings this lens to his buildings and clean energy work, ensuring that pursuing a clean energy future does not increase existing social injustices or energy inequities. He states that 'it is not enough for us to pursue a clean energy future that increases injustices that we have today,' and instead aims for an equitable and clean energy future.
149cd7c087.e: High-Tech Sunday: Ep. 52 - Roderick Jackson, Ph.D.

c0b042d573.q: What does clean energy mean and why is transitioning away from coal-based electricity generation important?
c0b042d573.a: Clean energy means generating electricity without relying on dirty fossil fuels like coal and natural gas. When coal is burned to generate electricity, it creates smoke and soot that is emitted into the atmosphere, trapping light and causing climate change. Clean energy replaces this fossil fuel-based generation with renewable sources that do not produce these harmful emissions.
c0b042d573.e: High-Tech Sunday: Ep. 52 - Roderick Jackson, Ph.D.

8ede939ad0.q: How did Dr. Jackson's spirituality influence his pursuit of a PhD in mechanical engineering?
8ede939ad0.a: Dr. Jackson's spirituality served as a foundation during the difficult PhD process. He cited First Corinthians, stating 'by the grace of God, I am what I am' and noted that while he worked hard—studying in the lab while others socialized—it was still by the grace of God that he had the will to persevere. His spiritual grounding helped him during stressful moments when he questioned whether the PhD was for him, knowing he had 'something within me that is bigger than this current stressful situation.'
8ede939ad0.e: High-Tech Sunday: Ep. 52 - Roderick Jackson, Ph.D.

7553e5a3a0.q: How did Clayton Turner become Director of NASA Langley Research Center?
7553e5a3a0.a: After graduating high school, Turner initially struggled in college, spent three years in the Army, then worked repairing pinball machines and video games before working at Dynamic Recording Studio in Rochester, New York. While in Rochester during a blizzard, he decided to return to college with greater motivation. Upon graduation, he received a call on his birthday from someone inviting him to interview at NASA Langley Research Center, where he was born on Langley Air Force Base. The combination of mentorship and guided opportunities throughout his career—rather than a deliberate plan to become center director—led him to progressively take…

c9e638c9ea.q: What skills did Clayton Turner develop through unconventional early jobs that prepared him for leadership at NASA?
c9e638c9ea.a: In the Army, Turner learned servant leadership. Working on pinball machines, video games, and jukeboxes taught him problem-solving and asking deeper questions about sustainability. At Dynamic Recording Studio, he initially expected to work alone with dials and knobs, but learned that 'it's all about the human beings. The dials and knobs are just table stakes.' He realized his job was to get the best out of people. These experiences directly prepared him for his current role: 'My job right now today is to create an environment where amazingly brilliant people can do amazing things.'

ad26546ccb.q: What does 'feed your fear or feed your faith' mean in Clayton Turner's leadership philosophy?
ad26546ccb.a: Turner uses this phrase—taught to him by his uncle—to describe how people face challenges and opportunities. He sees doubt and fear as 'the enemy trying to take you off the path that's for you.' People can either feed their fear by accepting doubt, or feed their faith that challenges are preparing them for opportunities. Turner applied this when invited to join the office of director, overcoming self-doubt by letting go of his own understanding and trusting in a larger purpose, which he describes as 'reaching for new heights to reveal the unknown for the benefit of humankind.'

e69af8eb5b.q: Why did a young girl tell her teacher in 2017 that she could not be an astronaut?
e69af8eb5b.a: During an event where Turner brought a colleague dressed in an astronaut suit, a young girl was later told by her teacher she would play the astronaut role in a recreation activity. The girl responded: 'I can't be an astronaut because I'm a girl.' Turner notes this occurred in 2017, not in the 1940s or 1950s, and uses it as an example of how artificial 'I can'ts' get planted in children's heads. He emphasizes the need to 'fill them up with some I cans and balance it off' to counter these limiting beliefs.

23c76e2290.q: What is the meaning of 'hard does not equal impossible' in Clayton Turner's philosophy?
23c76e2290.a: Turner explains that people often artificially equate 'hard' and 'impossible' as the same thing. He illustrates this with a story about seeing a full-scale projection of the Saturn V rocket on the Washington Monument, where thousands gathered 50 years after the event. He notes that flying was once only for 'crazy daredevils,' but the impossible became possible through hard work. Turner emphasizes: 'hard means just hard work to get there, but it does not mean impossible.'

b794eae135.q: How does Clayton Turner develop 'I cans' at NASA Langley Research Center?
b794eae135.a: Turner uses multiple strategies: being present in communities locally, across the state, region, and country to share the message that possibilities exist; traveling to cities and schools to talk with students and share NASA materials; mentoring through formal programs like the Patty Grace Foundation, which provides executive and peer mentors to college students; and emphasizing that everyone in any profession—engineers, scientists, accountants, lawyers—can contribute to making 'the magic' happen, not just specialized roles.
